items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: So I mean I was offered Count Basie’s band, when I was with Maynard’s band

ctx.x: Well I’m jealous of some of your playing experiences, because I often times think I was born a little too late. But we’re both still here. And I’m going to remember that answer.

Yeah because I’d be gone, long gone. But man I can’t say that I have an awful lot of regrets in life. I mean my life ambition in high school was to someday play with Woody Herman’s band and Maynard Ferguson’s band. And I had achieved both of that when I was 27. So I mean I was offered Count Basie’s band, when I was with Maynard’s band, and I said — I was offered that twice I think and I turned it — I am kind of regretful that I turned it down. Although I do have a feeling that the intensity that I was playing and…

I find that fascinating, this idea of playing on top of the beat. How can you — I heard Louis Hayes one night at some club and I said, “he is so on top of this beat, how does this music not speed up?” Or maybe it does.
